newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mostly up but jet lower, fuel flat.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mostly up but jet lower, fuel flat.

text.p: European oil swaps were mostly higher on Thursday morning, with gasoline showing the strongest gains but fuel oil flat and jet seeing another decline.
Brent CFDs gained ground after a cargo of Brent traded at five cents under September or the equivalent of 15 cents under October.
Next week's dates rose about five cents to 24 cents under October, while the following three weeks were all firmer at about 23 cents under.
Monthly CFDs showed little changed against the front line IPE. Discounts to the screen were around 28 cents (Sept), 27 cents (Oct), 20 cents (4Q97) and 11 cents (1Q97).
Heavy fuel swaps were flat after giving up early gains due to firmer Singapore prices. High sulphur barges talked $95.75 for September by midday, having peaked 50 cents around mid-morning.
The market remained in gentle contango and low sulphur was well bid for September at $100 a tonne.
"The high-low (spreads) firmed on the front end," said a broker who heard $5.25 a tonne trade for the fourth quarter.
Fourth barges were valued around $98.50 with low sulphur at $103.75.

Gas oil cracks against Brent crude were initially seen as steady as they had been all week, but the strong late morning gains on the IPE screen saw brokers notionally revising cracks higher for front months at least.
A fourth quarter trade on jet differentials at $24.25 underlined yet another $0.25 drop for forward months and outer quarters, mirroring early losses seen on the previous two days of trading.
EN590 and 0.2 diesel differentials were also expected to face some renewed pressure during the course of the day, although there was too little early talk to indicate an immediate decline.
Gasoline swaps jumped by another $4 on August to around $222 and by $3.50 on September to $203-$204 in early trading as a Sept/Oct spread trade was seen at $11.
The jump was seen linked to Tuesday's NYMEX gains and to a prompt barge market that saw early Thursday trades $9-$10 above late Wednesday values.
The September gasoline crack to Brent was latest seen offered at 5.10, slightly lower than late Wednesday's 5.20 talk but still much higher than late Tuesday/early Wednesday offers around 4.20.

The NYMEX and European gasoline strengthening, strong trader bidding on physical naphtha and early IPE crude futures gains were seen pushing up naphtha swaps values by $1.50-$2 on August and September to $194-$195 and $189-$190 respectively, dealers said.
